source.title: Understanding and Controlling a Maze-Solving Policy Network
source.authors: Ulisse Mini; Peli Grietzer; Mrinank Sharma; Austin Meek; M. MacDiarmid; A. M. Turner

record.tranche_reason: The study reports results about goal-tracking channels in a small maze-solving reinforcement-learning network, but it does not test neuron-pole job counts, explanations on held-out activations, or attribution graphs in language models.
record.gate_note: The study identifies and intervenes on residual channels, not neuron poles or language-model neuron explanations. Its channel findings are recorded with versions ["none"]; none of V1–V7 names the maze-policy setting or the specific channel measurements. The paper also reports behavioral statistics about goal pursuit, but these concern a maze policy rather than the claimed neuron interpretability measures.
record.test_reason: The study analyses residual channels of a 3.5M-parameter convolutional maze-solving RL policy. It identifies 11 channels that track cheese location and steers the policy through activation edits. It does not measure the share of neurons or neuron poles with one main job in any language model or vision model. It also does not test the cat-and-car neuron or pose explanation, does not compare tools or architectures for interpretable-unit share, and does not build neuron attribution graphs. It does not score explanations on held-out activations or by simulation. The 11-of-128 count comes from visually searching for one feature (cheese location). It is not an audit of how many channels have a single coherent role, so it cannot stand in for V1, V2 or V4. The paper does not cite or engage the original sources; 'discusses' is a loose fit, since the study neither tests nor uses the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the policy pursues multiple context-dependent goals; 11 channels track cheese location; activation edits and steering vectors partially control it; goal representations are redundant, distributed and retargetable.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies residual-channel identification, resampling, and activation steering in a maze-policy network, rather than language-model neuron-pole explanation or attribution-graph evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: Retargeting effectiveness depends on target location: it decreases farther from the historical top-right path. Resampling behavior also differs between same-cheese and random/different-cheese conditions.

fits_no_version.finding: In a maze-solving RL policy, 11 of 128 residual channels at one layer track cheese location. Resampling or editing them partially controls behaviour: 40% vs 11% action changes; path probability 0.695 vs 0.647 for all-channel vs single-channel edits. Moving the actual cheese retargets the policy more strongly, implying additional unidentified cheese circuitry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Goal-location information in this maze policy is redundantly distributed across several residual channels, which give partial but incomplete causal control over goal pursuit.

record.problems: The channel identification is described as visual inspection. Quantitative resampling results are reported for the first 30 maze seeds in Table 8, and the paper notes that these results were weaker than expected under its full channel hypothesis. Several intervention comparisons are described in text but their exact plotted values are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Not all individual qualitative maze examples and figures were recorded; they illustrate the same channel-resampling or activation-steering effects already represented in the rows (Sections 2.2–3.2 and Appendices C–E).

untested.parts: All: shares across dense and MoE language models and scale.
All: InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron, pose, recursive generalization vs superposition.
All: interpretable-unit share as a function of architecture, regularization and tools.
All: neuron-based attribution graphs vs replacement models in a large model.
All: whether explanations from activating examples predict firing elsewhere.
All: simulation-based automated scoring of neuron explanations.

record.verdict_notes: The study is out of scope for every version: wrong system type (RL conv policy), wrong unit (spatial residual channels), and no interpretable-share audit. The maze-behaviour regression results (82.4% accuracy vs a 71.4% baseline) are also unrelated to the claim and need no rows here.

versions.untested_parts: Qwen3-32B neuron-pole job shares and explanation testing on activations not used to write explanations.
Neuron-pole shares across language models, dense or mixture-of-experts architectures, or model scales.
InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose, and recursive generalization.
Architecture, regularization, tool quality, and interpretability-share estimates for vision models.
Attribution graphs in a large model, explanation of its behavior, and comparison with a trained replacement model or its reconstruction error.
Whether explanations fit to activating examples predict firing on other examples.
Automated simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations on new text.

rows.subject: maze-solving policy network (n = 5)
rows.stage_stated: pretrained; trained by Langosco et al. (2023) using PPO
rows.operation_detail: Visually inspected residual channels for activation patterns tracking cheese location.

conditions.value: after the first residual block of the second IMPALA block

rows.measure: Number of channels visually found to track cheese location
rows.note: These are spatial residual channels, not individual neuron poles. The authors describe the goal representation as redundant.
rows.check: Measures how many channels track one targeted feature, found by visual inspection. It is not the share of units with one main job, so it bears on no version despite looking superficially like V1/V4.

rows.operation_detail: Resampled activations of the 11 cheese-tracking channels from another maze and measured changes to the most probable action at a decision square.
rows.measure: Share of cases in which the most probable action at a decision square changed
rows.note: The comparison condition had a lower reported change rate; the authors say the channels affect behavior mostly based on cheese location, but not exclusively.
